verdict.reasoning: Patient reports being short of breath: Doctor: "You said you're a bit short of breath, is that right?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah. Feeling very sort of breathless recently."
Patient describes pleuritic right-back pain with deep breaths: "whenever I like. Breathe deeply, it sort of catches in the right hand side of my back."
Patient reports feeling feverish: "Well, I've had. I've got a bit of a slight fever" and also "You said you felt a bit warmer."
Patient reports hemoptysis: "I coughed up a bit of blood on two occasions."
Acute symptoms for about a day: Doctor: "And how long has this been going on for now?" Patient: "Just. Just a day, really."
Deep breaths provoke right-sided back pain: "whenever I like. Breathe deeply, it sort of catches in the right hand side of my back."
Fatigue duration: "I've been feeling a bit like a bit tired at work..." Doctor: "And how long has that been ... ?" Patient: "Only for a couple of weeks or so."
Reduced exercise tolerance for ~2 weeks: "exercising has been a bit difficult because I've been feeling tired" and "Only for a couple of weeks or so."
Non-smoker: Doctor: "do you smoke at all?" Patient: "No."
No recent long-haul flights: Doctor: "Have you been on any long haul flight recently?" Patient: "No. No."
Lives alone in a flat: Doctor: "And do you live alone?" Patient: "Yes." Doctor: "In a flat or a house?" Patient: "Flat."
Desk job: Doctor: "What do you work as?" Patient: "I work in an office. Just a desk job."
Has a cat: Doctor: "Do you have any pets?" Patient: "Cats?" Doctor: "A cat. Okay."

Methotrexate for SLE and last dose today: Patient: "Yeah. Methotrexate." Doctor: "What are you on that for?" Patient: "I've got sle." Later: "When was the last time you had methotrexate?" Patient: "This morning."
Feeling warmer/feverish: Doctor: "You said you felt a bit warmer. Have you measured your temperature at all?" Patient had earlier said: "I've got a bit of a slight fever."
No prior blood clots: Doctor: "Have you ever had any clots in your legs or clots in your lungs, blood clots?" Patient: "Not that I know of, no."
No recent immobilization is not discussed anywhere in the transcript (no mention of immobility, recent surgery, or being bedbound).
History of SLE: Patient: "I've got sle." Doctor repeats: "Sle. Okay."
On methotrexate: Patient: "Yeah. Methotrexate. Methotrexate." Doctor: "Methotrexate. Okay."
Last methotrexate dose this morning: Doctor: "When was the last time you had methotrexate?" Patient: "This morning."
No allergies: Doctor: "do you have any allergies to any medication?" Patient: "No." Doctor: "Any other allergies at all?" Patient: "No."
Lives alone: Doctor: "And do you live alone?" Patient: "Yes."
Desk job: "I work in an office. Just a desk job."
Has a cat: "Do you have any pets?" Patient: "Cats?" Doctor: "A cat. Okay."

Pulse estimated 66–74 bpm and regular: Doctor times pulse and says, "that was about 11 or 12. So that would make your heart rate about 66 to 74. That's okay." Regularity implied by single pulse count and no concern.
Neck exam: Doctor instructs to feel neck glands; Patient: "No, they feel pretty normal to me." indicating no enlarged glands.
Patient did say "Ah" and doctor examined throat, but the transcript does not explicitly state that the oropharynx was normal-appearing; only "Perfect. Thank you for that. Excellent."

Capillary refill assessed and described as good: Doctor demonstrates and then says after patient performs it: "Okay, perfect. That's great. Thank you so much." and earlier: Patient: "You've got very good circulation." implying quick return of color.

No lung auscultation or imaging in this tele-visit and exam limited: Doctor notes need for in-person exam "someone needs to listen to your chest" and describes current online examination as limited: "from what limited examination I could do online"; no imaging or auscultation performed in transcript.
Temperature not objectively measured: Doctor asks, "Have you measured your temperature at all?" Patient: "With the back of my hand, yes." indicating no thermometer reading and only subjective fever.

Doctor suspects chest infection/pneumonia: "this sounds like you might have a chest infection" and later "we do need to assess you to figure out whether you have a pneumonia or chest infection" in context of cough with blood, pleuritic pain, fever, and acute onset.

Hemoptysis in context of possible infection and need to exclude cancer/other serious causes: Doctor reassures about lung cancer but says "we might need to get some investigations to exclude that" and mentions need for follow-up chest X-ray if things don’t settle, i.e., to exclude cancer and other causes.

While patient is on methotrexate for SLE (immunosuppressive), the doctor never explicitly states that immunosuppression increases infection risk or uses it in reasoning; this risk inference is clinical knowledge not mentioned in the transcript.

Fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance for ~2 weeks: patient notes tiredness and exercise difficulty, "performing daily activities has been a bit harder" and duration "Only for a couple of weeks or so."

Same-day in-person clinic visit with chest exam and vitals: "we'll arrange for you to get reviewed in a clinic today... listen to your chest and check your blood pressure and to recheck your pulse as well. Just make sure. Check your temperature".
Antibiotics considered if infection confirmed: "You may well need an antibiotic" and later links this to in-person assessment to figure out if pneumonia/chest infection is present.

Possible chest X-ray if symptoms persist to exclude cancer/other causes: "we may end up having to do a follow up chest X ray if things don't settle down" and in discussion of lung cancer and pneumonia as etiologies.
No antibiotics before evaluation: "I'm not going to prescribe anything for you now because I think you need to have that basic assessment first before we proceed to the next step."
Same-day face-to-face appointment via support team: "they will book you in for a face to face appointment with one of our GPS today" after patient calls support team number.
No explicit counseling on specific red flag symptoms such as increasing SOB, vertigo, confusion, chest pain, or fainting appears in the transcript.
Although methotrexate use and SLE are documented, the plan does not explicitly mention monitoring for infection specifically due to immunosuppression or adjusting the plan on that basis.
Same-day face-to-face follow-up arranged: "they will book you in for a face to face appointment with one of our GPS today" for further assessment.
